items.description: The Chairman of Parliament’s Select Committee on Youth and Sports, Ernest Henry Norgbey, has commended the Chief Executive Officer of the National Youth Authority (NYA), Osman Ayariga, and his management team for what he described as a “yeoman’s job” in keeping the Authority operational despite limited budgetary allocations. The Chairman of Parliament’s Select Committee on Youth and Sports, Ernest Henry Norgbey, has commended the Chief Executive Officer of the National Youth Authority (NYA), Osman Ayariga, and his management team for what he described as a “yeoman’s job” in keeping the Authority operational despite limited budgetary allocations. Mr Norgbey made the remarks on Thursday, October 8, 2026, when the Committee paid a working visit to the NYA and was received by Mr Ayariga, management and staff of the Authority. He said the Committee would work with the Authority to identify ways of addressing the challenges confronting it, particularly those linked to inadequate resources, to enable the government’s youth-focused programmes being implemented through the NYA to achieve their intended objectives. “With the best of our ability, we would see how best we can dissolve those challenges, so basically, the programmes that the government is implementing through the NYA will all see the light of day,” Mr Norgbey said. He commended the CEO and the technical staff for their commitment, saying their efforts were helping to keep the Authority on its feet despite the meagre budgetary allocation. “We can only say kudos to them for the work that they’re doing for Mother Ghana and the government as well,” he added.

items.title: Cinquante et un (51) jeunes, dont cinq (5) femmes, sont désormais formés à la conduite de poids lourds et de super poids lourds
items.description: La deuxième cohorte des élèves stagiaires de l'ASCAD a entamé son évaluation finale ce jeudi 06 octobre, marquant ainsi la fin de trois mois de formation dispensée avec l'appui du Groupe GUICOPRES. Le programme privilégiait la pratique, à hauteur de 70 %, contre 30 % de théorie. Cette formation s'inscrit dans un engagement de longue date. Sous l'impulsion de son Président Directeur Général, M. Kerfalla CAMARA, le Groupe accompagne l'ASCAD depuis plusieurs années dans la formation des jeunes. Dans le cadre de sa politique de responsabilité sociétale des entreprises (RSE), GUICOPRES envisage d'étendre cette collaboration à d'autres métiers, comme la plomberie, l'électricité ou l'entretien, en parfaite harmonie avec la vision du Président de la République, Son Excellence Mamadi Doumbouya, qui place la jeunesse au cœur de tous les projets de développement. Présents à la cérémonie, M. Karamo II KABA, Directeur Général Adjoint du Groupe GUICOPRES en charge des affaires administratives et juridiques, et M. Amadou Keïta, Directeur Général Adjoint de l'ASCAD, ont souligné chacun, l'excellence du partenariat entre les deux entités. Pour M. KABA, « l'ASCAD incarne une priorité présidentielle en matière de formation de la jeunesse guinéenne ». Il a rappelé l'attachement du PDG du Groupe à cette jeunesse, ce qui explique l'accompagnement de l'agence. « Au-delà de la formation, nous offrons à ceux qui se démarquent un véritable cadre professionnel au sein du Groupe », a-t-il ajouté. Du côté de l'ASCAD, M. Amadou Keïta a présenté GUICOPRES comme un partenaire qui contribue à la formation des jeunes vulnérables recrutés, en vue de leur insertion socio-professionnelle. « C'est un engagement que le Groupe a pris auprès de l'ASCAD et de la population guinéenne », a-t-il affirmé, en soulignant que cette démarche soutient la politique publique de l'État : faire de la qualification de la jeunesse une priorité. Il a qualifié cette collaboration de « première importance ». Le responsable a remercié le Groupe, son Président Kerfalla Camara, ainsi que l'ensemble de l'encadrement et des cadres techniques. « Dans le respect du contenu local, le Groupe investit dans la jeunesse guinéenne, et il faut que tout le monde le sache », a-t-il insisté. Selon lui, ce partenariat allège les charges de formation professionnelle de l'ASCAD et facilite l'insertion des jeunes : « GUICOPRES les accueille, les forme, puis en emploie une partie », dit-il. L'ASCAD se dit pleinement satisfaite, et les deux parties ont décidé, lors de leur dernière rencontre, d'élargir la collaboration à d'autres filières. Au nom des élèves, Mme Aissatou Keita a décrit un bénéfice incommensurable pour leurs futures carrières. « Je remercie GUICOPRES et l'ASCAD, ainsi que l'ensemble des responsables qui nous ont formés et pris soin de nous durant la formation », a-t-elle déclaré. Avec cette cohorte, GUICOPRES et l'ASCAD montrent qu'un partenariat entre une entreprise privée et une institution publique peut déboucher sur des perspectives concrètes pour la jeunesse : accueillir, former, puis employer. La présence de cinq femmes parmi les bénéficiaires illustre aussi l'ouverture d'un métier longtemps perçu comme masculin.

items.title: Importation des véhicules : ce qui pourrait changer pour les Algériens de la diaspora
items.description: Le projet de loi de finances pour 2027 propose des changements concernant l’importation de véhicules et de marchandises par les membres de la communauté nationale établie à l’étranger et les fonctionnaires du corps diplomatique en fin de mission à l’étranger. Retour définitif de la diaspora : du nouveau pour l’importation de véhicules La première proposition concerne l’importation de véhicules par les nationaux résidents à l'étranger à l’occasion de leur retour définitif en Algérie. En plus des types et catégories de véhicules qu'ils sont autorisés à importer avec des avantages fiscaux, l'article 159 du PLF 2027 propose d'intégrer les véhicules hybrides (essence et électrique) pour le transport des marchandises relevant de la position tarifaire n° 87.04, d'un poids total en charge n'excédant pas 5,950 tonnes, ou les véhicules à deux roues, relevant de la position tarifaire n° 87.11. La mesure va permettre d’harmoniser les conditions de bénéfice des avantages fiscaux applicables aux véhicules utilitaires et aux véhicules à deux roues avec celles prévues pour les véhicules de tourisme, notamment à travers l’introduction de critères techniques plus précis fondés sur les positions tarifaires, explique le gouvernement. Un taux unique sur les marchandises excédentaires Quant aux marchandises importées dans le même cadre et excédant les seuils fixés, elles sont admises au dédouanement en dispense des formalités du contrôle du commerce extérieur et des changes, moyennant l'acquittement d'une taxe forfaitaire unique au taux de 60 % de la valeur des marchandises en question. La même disposition bénéficie aux agents diplomatiques et consulaires et assimilés. L’objectif de la disposition est de simplifier les opérations de dédouanement des marchandises importées dans ce cadre, à “garantir une application uniforme et transparente de la réglementation et à renforcer la sécurité juridique tant pour les personnes bénéficiaires que pour les services des douanes”. S’agissant de l’importation de véhicules par les agents diplomatiques et consulaires et assimilés, à leur rappel définitif en fin de mission à l’extérieur, les véhicules à deux roues, dont la valeur n'excède pas dix millions de dinars, sont intégrés dans la liste des véhicules autorisés à l’importation avec des avantages douaniers. L’article Importation des véhicules : ce qui pourrait changer pour les Algériens de la diaspora est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Mahama commends Trade Minister for championing Ghana’s industrial growth
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has commended Trade, Agribusiness and Industry Minister Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare for her active engagement with businesses and efforts to address challenges confronting Ghana’s manufacturing and industrial sectors. He said the Minister’s close engagement with industry players had helped the government better understand and respond to operational challenges affecting businesses. President Mahama made the remarks on Thursday, October 8, 2026, when he visited the Kasapreko Plc manufacturing facility in Accra, where he praised the company’s expansion and contribution to job creation and industrial development. He said the decision to redesignate the Ministry of Trade as the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry was intended to broaden its mandate and give the industrial sector a stronger voice within government. “Previously, trade was virtually the only engagement the Ministry was involved in. But now industries have a voice in their Ministry, and happily, they have a Minister who is hardworking and energetic, so they take all their complaints to her,” President Mahama said. The President cited the Minister’s interventions in addressing challenges affecting manufacturers, including water supply, land acquisition and other constraints to industrial expansion. The remarks come as government continues to emphasise stronger collaboration with the private sector as part of efforts to drive industrialisation and economic transformation. President Mahama has previously said his administration is targeting an increase in manufacturing’s contribution to GDP to at least 15 per cent by 2030, supported by new industrial jobs. Madam Ofosu-Adjare expressed gratitude to President Mahama for his commitment and personal support towards the growth and transformation of Ghana’s industrial sector. She described the President as the “Commander-in-Chief of Industry”, acknowledging his efforts to create an enabling environment for businesses to expand production, attract investment and create jobs. “The President gives us support to industry. He is there personally to lend support, and we see the level at which he is bringing industry forward, making sure that we do not only produce for import substitution but also produce for export,” she said. The Chief Executive Officer of Kasapreko Plc, Richard Adjei, also commended the Minister for her interventions in addressing challenges relating to water supply, power, cross-border trade and other operational difficulties confronting manufacturers. He particularly cited her role in facilitating an extension of the period for exporters to repatriate export proceeds from 60 to 90 days, describing the measure as important support for businesses seeking to expand their export operations. “Since she came, I must say that we have taken a lot of complaints to her from Ghana Water, power issues and cross-border issues, and she has been very helpful,” he said. Kasapreko’s growth has also been highlighted as an example of the potential of Ghanaian-owned businesses to expand and access long-term capital. The company raised GH¢1.72 billion through its Initial Public Offering earlier in 2026 and subsequently listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange.

items.title: Public cautioned against transactions over Borteyman land as Supreme Court rules in favour of Sino Africa
items.description: People who acquired and developed portions of disputed land at Borteyman, Tema, in the Greater Accra Region have been asked to submit their title documents to Sino Africa Development Company Limited following a Supreme Court ruling in the company’s favour, subject to exceptions protecting two other companies. In a public notice issued on October 8, 2026, Sino Africa requested that those who acquired interests in the land before June 3, 2026, and have built on or developed it contact the company or its solicitors within 30 days for clarification of how the judgment affects their acquisitions. The company also warned prospective buyers against purchasing or leasing portions of the affected land from five defendants in the case or anyone claiming through them. According to the notice, the Supreme Court delivered its judgment on June 3, 2026, overturning the majority decision of the Court of Appeal dated March 27, 2025. The case, Civil Appeal No. J4/44/2025, concerns two parcels at Borteyman, also known as Nungua Farms, in Tema in the Greater Accra Region. Together, the parcels cover approximately 328.877 acres. The notice states that the court declared title in Sino Africa’s favour, except for the parcel claimed by Royal Bell Investments Limited and Terraform Development Limited, the first and second defendants. Sino Africa’s entitlement to recover possession is also subject to the possessory rights of those two companies. “The Plaintiff/Appellant/Appellant shall be entitled to recover possession of the land claimed as the legal title owner, subject to the possessory right of the 1st and 2nd Defendants/Respondents/Respondents,” the notice quotes the judgment as stating. The other defendants named in the case are Nii Adzogah Annang Laryea, Nii Odaifio Mensah, Nii Asafoatse Okum Agyemang II, Richard Nii Alabi Bortey and Benjamin Borketey Borteye Seysey. The notice reports that the court imposed a perpetual restraint on those five defendants and persons claiming through them concerning interference with the land declared in Sino Africa’s favour. The company consequently cautioned the public against buying, leasing, accepting grants or otherwise dealing in the affected land through those parties. “Any person who does so after the date of this Notice does so with full notice of the judgment of the Supreme Court and entirely at his or her own risk,” it stated. Existing developers covered by the notice are requested to provide copies of their title documents when contacting the company or its solicitors. The 30-day period is a request contained in Sino Africa’s notice, which describes its purpose as clarifying the judgment and its effects on earlier acquisitions. The company said a certified true copy of the judgment and a site plan of the land could be inspected at its solicitors’ offices during normal working hours. No stipulation in Makkah pact bars 'direct involvement' in case of threat to a member: Asif
items.description: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said on Thursday that no stipulation of the Makkah Defence Alliance barred the member states from getting “directly involved” in case of a threat to one of the members. He said this during ARY News programme ‘ Khabar Muhammad Malick Ke Saath ’ after he was asked about the possibility of Pakistan sending ground troops to Yemen amid an escalating conflict between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia under the alliance, which comprises Islamabad, Riyadh and Ankara. “To defend one of the member countries, the remaining two would get involved as if they are defending themselves,” he added. The Makkah defence pact was signed on Aug 7 to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. It has gained relevance amid renewed fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis. On Monday, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agreed to the rapid deployment of military forces and capabilities in the kingdom during an emergency meeting of the Makkah Defence Alliance in Riyadh, which was held to address the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia. A statement issued by the Foreign Office after the moot said the member states had “decided to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the kingdom, in accordance with the approved arrangements and the national legislation of the parties, thereby enhancing readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats”. Separately, Asif, who was part of Pakistan’s delegation in the meeting, joined Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’ via telephone the same day and said Pakistan and Turkiye had a “presence in theatre”, but only Saudi troops were involved in combat operations. On Wednesday, Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry also said Pakistani troops were in Saudi Arabia, adding that they had been in the kingdom “for decades” and across multiple domains. Earlier, on Sept 18, Lt Gen Chaudhry also said Pakistan would go to “any extent” to defend the Gulf state, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security is “unconditional”. Asif has also reaffirmed that Pakistan will “practically and diplomatically” stand by Saudi Arabia against Yemen’s Houthi rebels if the situation escalates. The defence minister said that Pakistan would fulfil all its obligations under the Makkah Defence Alliance in accordance with the terms of the agreement between the three countries. At the same time, Pakistan has also asserted that the alliance is intended for collective deterrence and is defensive in nature. Meanwhile, the information ministry has dismissed a news report claiming that Pakistan Air Force aircraft were being used against Yemen’s Houthis as “fake and fabricated”. Earlier this week, the ministry also termed a Reuters report claiming the deployment of 30,000 to 40,000 Pakistani troops in Saudi Arabia as “speculative”.

items.title: Minority demands permanent scrapping of GSA’s $300 PVoC charge on imported vehicles
items.description: The Minority in Parliament has called on the Ghana Standards Authority (GSA) to permanently scrap its proposed Pre-shipment Verification of Conformity (PVoC) requirement for imported vehicles, arguing that the policy would increase costs for importers and consumers. Michael Okyere Baafi, Ranking Member of Parliament’s Trade and Industry Committee, said the decision to suspend implementation of the policy was not enough and urged the GSA to withdraw it completely. Speaking to the media on Thursday, October 8, Mr Baafi said Ghana imports slightly more than 100,000 vehicles annually, with between 70% and 80% being used and overage vehicles. He said the proposed requirement, which includes a reported US$300 verification charge, would place an additional burden on importers already facing rising costs and other challenges at the ports. “Ghana imports a little over 100,000 vehicles every year. Seventy to 80 per cent of these imported vehicles are overage and used vehicles,” he said. According to Mr Baafi, importers would have to engage an agent to verify their vehicles before shipment to Ghana and pay US$300 before a certificate could be issued. He said the additional cost would eventually be passed on to consumers through higher vehicle prices. Minority wants permanent withdrawal Mr Baafi said the GSA should scrap the policy rather than suspend it, arguing that a suspension could leave room for the requirement to be reintroduced later. “We think that the Ghana Standards Authority should withdraw this policy immediately, not get suspension. It’s not enough,” he said. He maintained that existing mechanisms were available to determine whether vehicles entering the country were stolen and questioned the need for another verification process that would increase costs. “It’s a policy that is completely not necessary at this time. The economy is not too good. You know that people are going through a lot of issues,” he said. Concern over vehicle prices Mr Baafi said the proposed charge would come on top of import duties and other costs associated with bringing vehicles into the country. He noted that Ghana’s vehicle assembly industry remained limited, meaning many middle-class Ghanaians continued to rely on imported vehicles. “We are bound to still go for imported vehicles,” he said. He questioned how importers already struggling with the cost of doing business would absorb another mandatory payment. “Where are they going to get money to even pay import duties when they come?” he asked. Mr Baafi also cited complaints from traders, vehicle importers and freight forwarders about taxes and levies, congestion and the broader cost of doing business at the ports. “Traders are complaining. Importers and freight forwarders are complaining of hardship at the port, unnecessary taxes and levies, and congestion at the port. You are going to add up this,” he said. Bawumia pledge Mr Baafi also linked the issue to the New Patriotic Party’s plans, saying former Vice-President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia had indicated that the policy would be scrapped if the NPP returned to power. He said he and Dr Bawumia recently met representatives of the Ghana Union of Traders Association (GUTA), during which he claimed Dr Bawumia pledged to abolish the policy if elected President in 2028. Mr Baafi said the Minority would continue to push for the PVoC requirement to be permanently withdrawn. “The suspension is not enough,” he said. “They should scrap it.”

items.title: Les véritables complaintes des usagers de Ziguinchor
items.description: Les usagers de Sen’Eau ont profité d’une rencontre organisée ce jeudi 08 octobre 2026 avec la direction territoriale sud pour mettre sur la table tout haut ce qu’ils vivent au quotidien. À Ziguinchor comme dans les zones rurales, les plaintes portent surtout sur les factures jugées élevées, les coupures d’eau et les difficultés d’accès à une eau disponible et de qualité. ZIGUINCHOR- La rencontre organisée ce jeudi 8 octobre par la direction territoriale sud de Sen’Eau a été l’occasion pour des délégués et représentants de quartiers de faire part de leurs préoccupations. Devant les responsables de la société, les consommateurs ont évoqué les difficultés liées à la fourniture d’eau, mais aussi le manque d’information lors des coupures. Venu de Tenghory, dans le département de Bignona, Alexandre Coly a insisté sur les difficultés rencontrées dans les zones rurales. « La disponibilité de l’eau reste un sérieux problème en milieu rural. Nous demandons à la Sen’Eau de renforcer les branchements sociaux afin de permettre à toutes les populations d’avoir accès à une eau de qualité. Nous voulons de l’eau en quantité et en qualité », suggère M. Coly. À Ziguinchor, Idrissa Diallo, délégué de quartier, dénonce surtout les coupures sans préavis. « Les coupures d’eau se font parfois sans que les clients ne soient informés. Les usagers doivent être prévenus à temps, avant les interruptions. La Sen’Eau doit aussi veiller à fournir une eau de qualité aux consommateurs », déplore-t-il. Face à ces préoccupations, la direction territoriale sud assure vouloir renforcer le dialogue avec les populations. Directeur territorial de la zone sud, Oumar Sarr, explique que cette rencontre entre dans le cadre de la « politique 2026-2028 » de ladite société. « Nous avons fait de l’ancrage territorial l’un des axes importants de notre politique. Pour cela, il faut aller à la rencontre des consommateurs, de recueillir leurs besoins, leurs réclamations et leurs plaintes, au lieu de rester uniquement dans nos bureaux », explique-t-il. Concernant les baisses de pression signalées dans certains quartiers de Ziguinchor, le responsable cite Djibock, Kénia et les zones d’extension. « Ce sont principalement ces zones hautes qui connaissent des baisses de pression. Mais un programme de renforcement du réseau est actuellement en cours pour améliorer la situation », rassure Oumar Sarr. Sur la qualité de l’eau, il reconnaît les difficultés qui existaient auparavant, notamment la présence de fer et de boue de fer. Mais selon lui, la situation s’est nettement améliorée. « Jusqu’au premier trimestre 2025, nous avions beaucoup de fer et des difficultés à traiter toute l’eau provenant des forages. Aujourd’hui, ce problème est derrière nous. L’eau rougeâtre n’est plus un phénomène permanent à Ziguinchor. Elle peut toutefois apparaître ponctuellement après des réparations ou des opérations d’entretien », précise Oumar Sarr. Ainsi, l’entrevue a permis aux consommateurs de faire entendre leurs doléances et à la Sen’Eau de présenter les réponses envisagées. Mais, pour les usagers, l’enjeu reste désormais simple : avoir de l’eau, en quantité et en qualité, au moment où ils en ont besoin. Gaustin DIATTA (Correspondant)

items.title: Motsepe assure que la CAN 2027 aura bien lieu au Kenya, en Tanzanie et en Ouganda
items.description: Le président de la Confédération africaine de football (CAF), Patrice Motsepe, a confirmé, jeudi au Cap-Vert, que la Coupe d'Afrique des Nations (CAN) 2027 se tiendra bien comme prévu au Kenya, en Tanzanie et en Ouganda, malgré les inquiétudes concernant les préparatifs de la compétition. « Nous irons au Kenya, en Tanzanie et en Ouganda, nous aurons la CAN la plus réussie » , a affirmé Motsepe lors de la Conférence stratégique de la CAF, qui se tient du 7 au 9 octobre à Santa Maria, sur l'île de Sal, en présence notamment du président de la Fédération internationale de football (FIFA), Gianni Infantino. Le président de la CAF a, à cet égard, assuré s'être convaincu du « profond engagement » des chefs d'État des trois pays organisateurs en faveur de la réussite de cette compétition, indiquant avoir rencontré le président kényan, William Ruto, et la présidente tanzanienne, Samia Suluhu Hassan, dans le cadre du suivi des préparatifs du tournoi. Le Kenya, la Tanzanie et l'Ouganda avaient été désignés conjointement pour accueillir la CAN 2027, une première pour la compétition organisée dans trois pays. La Conférence stratégique de la CAF réunit les présidents des 54 associations membres, les présidents des unions zonales, les membres du Comité exécutif de l'instance continentale, des sélectionneurs, des responsables techniques et des experts internationaux. Cette rencontre est consacrée notamment à la définition des orientations pour le développement du football africain, au renforcement des associations membres et à l'analyse des performances des sélections du continent lors de la Coupe du Monde 2026. The post Motsepe assure que la CAN 2027 aura bien lieu au Kenya, en Tanzanie et en Ouganda appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: India's 'Cockroach' movement says many members detained ahead of Delhi rally
items.description: Indian authorities started mass detentions of people associated with the “Cockroach” youth movement, the group said on Thursday, just days ahead of a major planned protest in Delhi to demand the resignation of the nation’s top poll official. Opposition parties, their student units, and the “Cockroach” youth movement have been holding almost daily demonstrations seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over a controversial revision of voter lists . Many activists from across the country and a senior member and spokesperson of the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), Deepak Baliyan, were among those arrested, the movement and its leaders said on social media platform X. Police authorities didn’t immediately respond to Reuters ’ requests for comments. Videos posted on social media platform X showed activists being taken away in vans. Reuters could not immediately verify the claims or videos posted on X. The CJP said that among those detained was a group of students from the Western city of Pune who were headed for the October 10 protest in Delhi. It said they were being taken away in a bus to an unknown location. “Why not just declare emergency?”, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said in a response to a post with a video of activists being detained. New political challenge for Modi Opposition parties and the CJP have accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of using a revision of voter lists to fix them in its favour, in collusion with its appointees, including Kumar. The protests present a new political challenge to Modi midway into his third term, just months after similar demonstrations led by the CJP forced the resignation of his education minister over exam paper leaks. Kumar has not commented but the Election Commission and the BJP have denied the allegations. Indian social media influencer and activist Dhruv Rathee, Indian actor Prakash Raj, Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and other supporters gesture during a protest demanding the resignation of the country’s election chief Gyanesh Kumar, in Bengaluru, India, October 8, 2026. — Reuters Earlier in the day, hundreds of supporters of the CJP youth movement protested in tech hub Bengaluru. Many of the protesters held posters that said, “Every name counts, Every vote matters” and “Stop the Murder of Democracy”. “I think voting right is the most basic point of democracy … People who actually want to vote, who actually care about the future of India, they are just being (denied) voting rights,” Khushi Shrivastava, a 22-year-old architecture student who attended the Bengaluru protest, told Reuters . Supporters of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) attend a protest demanding the resignation of India’s Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in Bengaluru, India, October 8, 2026. — Reuters Visuals from news agency ANI showed dozens of Congress supporters staging a protest march on Thursday in ​the southern state of Telangana, while the opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal organised a similar demonstration in ​the eastern state of Bihar. Anger over detention of politicians There were also protests over police action against Congress party leaders and the voter lists revisions. On ⁠Wednesday, Congress accused police of using “brute force” to briefly detain party leader Rahul Gandhi, his sister Priyanka Vadra, and other lawmakers as they tried to ​reach the Jantar Mantar protest site in New Delhi. Delhi Police said the ​allegations were being ⁠used to “defame” the force. Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi sits inside a bus as he heads towards Rajghat during a protest organized by opposition parties demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India, October 8, 2026. — Reuters “We are on the ground and, as officers, we also ensure that every kind of legal duty is followed and no illegal, unnecessary actions take place,” senior police officer Shrishti Pandey ⁠told ANI . BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia said the allegations were “being levelled by an irresponsible, anarchist opposition”. The claims had “no base, not an iota of evidence”, he told reporters at a media briefing on Thursday.

items.description: « Des infos perso du chef du gouvernement sont parties dans les meandres d'internet », a rapporte le 7 octobre l'hebdomadaire satirique Le Canard enchaîne , assurant qu'« on tombe egalement assez facilement sur son 06 ». France Travail, Urssaf, education nationale, Agence nationale des titres securises (ANTS), Bloctel et meme le fisc : depuis des mois, les piratages d'agences etatiques ainsi que de ministeres se multiplient en France, defrayant la chronique et exposant les donnees de millions de Francais. Mi-août, apres que l'administration fiscale a reconnu avoir subi un piratage deux mois plus tot et que le hackeur a annonce la mise en vente des donnees volees sur le darknet, Matignon avait indique que Lecornu avait « demande a l'ANSSI [l'Agence nationale de la securite des systemes d'information] de conduire un audit approfondi pour etablir precisement les circonstances et les causes de l'incident ». Des piratages en serie, depeints comme une « veritable hemorragie » par des acteurs du secteur, qui n'epargnent pas l'executif. En effet, toujours selon le Palmipede, « des elements cles de la vie privee », tels que les numeros de telephone, les adresses et meme les identifiants bancaires de 25 membres du gouvernement — qui en compte 36 — se « baladent sur le Net » en raison de cyberattaques.

items.title: Situation politique en Guinée-Bissau : Le Sénégal appelle à la retenue et au respect du calendrier électoral
items.description: Face aux menaces qui pèsent sur les élections prévues le 6 décembre 2026 en Guinée-Bissau, la diplomatie sénégalaise invite les autorités de transition au dialogue et demande la levée des restrictions sur les activités politiques. Le gouvernement du Sénégal a exprimé ce jeudi 08 octobre 2026 sa vive attention quant aux récents développements politiques en République de Guinée-Bissau. Dans un communiqué rendu public le 08 octobre 2026, la diplomatie sénégalaise est sortie du silence face aux incertitudes qui entourent l'organisation des élections générales initialement fixées au 6 décembre 2026. Prenant acte des déclarations des autorités bissau-guinéennes relatives à des « contraintes juridiques, techniques et institutionnelles » pouvant retarder le scrutin, Dakar a tenu à fixer une ligne claire. Pour les autorités sénégalaises, toute révision de l'agenda électoral devra obligatoirement résulter d'un accord politique consenti par l'ensemble des acteurs. Le ministère des Affaires étrangères souligne que « toute modification du calendrier électoral doit s'inscrire dans une démarche consensuelle, inclusive et transparente, assortie de garanties claires quant à l'achèvement de la transition dans les meilleurs délais ». Afin de garantir la crédibilité du processus, le Sénégal formule la levée des restrictions pesant sur les activités politiques et civiles pour instaurer un climat de confiance, l’ouverture immédiate d'un dialogue constructif entre les autorités de transition, les forces politiques et la société civile bissau-guinéenne et l’appel à la retenue adressé à toutes les parties prenantes, en particulier aux responsables militaires, pour préserver la paix civile et éviter toute escalade. Rappelant le rôle central de Dakar, le communiqué insiste sur le double statut du Sénégal en tant que « pays assurant la présidence en exercice de la CEDEAO et de médiateur en Guinée-Bissau ». Dakar réaffirme sa volonté d'œuvrer en concertation étroite avec les États membres et les partenaires internationaux dans le respect de la souveraineté nationale et des aspirations démocratiques du peuple bissau-guinéen. Le gouvernement a conclu en réitérant sa « solidarité fraternelle » et sa détermination à accompagner la recherche d’une solution garantissant une stabilité institutionnelle durable. A.N

items.title: Why America Can’t Fully Escape an Oil Crisis
items.description: This is an edition of Time-Travel Thursdays, a journey through The Atlantic ’s archives to contextualize the present. Sign up here. In December 1987, The Atlantic had some reassuring news for readers: The next oil crisis didn’t have to happen. The United States had already endured the oil shocks of the 1970s, and Amory B. Lovins and L. Hunter Lovins, a pair of then-married environmentalists, argued in this magazine that the country had learned from the experience. The U.S. had diversified its sources of foreign oil, and the American economy needed less oil to grow, a shift that the Lovinses attributed mainly to efficiency gains, such as better-insulated buildings and more fuel-efficient cars. Oil production had grown outside OPEC, an organization of oil-exporting states, reducing the world’s reliance on Persian Gulf oil. Even the Strait of Hormuz, a flash point in the Iran-Iraq War of the ’80s, appeared less threatening to the global supply. By 1987, less oil was passing through the waterway than earlier in the decade, and the Lovinses believed that reserves and alternative routes could help make up for any sudden cutoffs caused by geopolitical tensions. The moment offered what the writers called a “unique opportunity”: a reprieve from Middle Eastern dominance of the global oil supply. “If this interval is frittered away,” they warned, “it could end with the United States, its alternative options expired, needing Middle Eastern oil more than ever.” Nearly four decades later, America is far less vulnerable to foreign-oil disruptions, but it is once again caught in a global oil crisis, and the Strait of Hormuz is back at the center. Before the Iran war, about a quarter of the world’s maritime oil passed through the strait, roughly three times the daily volume that had passed through in 1987. The effective closure of the waterway has resulted in global oil inventories falling by more than 500 million barrels since February , and Americans are feeling the effects, as the costs of diesel , air travel , food , and other goods all rise. But not all of the Lovinses’ worries have come to pass. America has become far less reliant on foreign oil than it was in the ’80s; the shale boom, precipitated by advances in horizontal drilling and hydraulic fracturing, unlocked large amounts of domestic oil, transforming the U.S. energy market beginning in the 2000s. Last year, American crude production reached a record 13.6 million barrels a day, and Persian Gulf countries supplied just 8 percent of U.S. crude imports. The contrast with the 1970s is stark: In 1977, the broader group of OPEC countries supplied 85 percent of American crude-oil imports. As my colleague Rogé Karma reported in March , America’s growing energy independence appears to have helped convince the Trump administration ahead of the Iran war that the U.S. could withstand a disruption in the Persian Gulf. “We don’t get any oil anymore out of the Strait of Hormuz,” Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said last October, in defense of America’s decision to strike Iran’s nuclear facilities earlier that year. The Lovinses had imagined a different route to energy security. They called it “substitution”: reducing the need for oil overall by continuing to improve energy efficiency in buildings and vehicles, and replacing oil with natural gas or alternative fuels. They argued that efficiency could buy the country time to free itself from dependence on foreign oil. America ultimately achieved much of that goal, but by producing more oil rather than using less. After OPEC’s 1973 oil embargo, President Richard Nixon launched “Project Independence” with the goal of reducing the country’s reliance on foreign oil. Congress adopted new conservation measures , and Jimmy Carter made reducing energy consumption a centerpiece of his presidency, while also beginning to lift federal controls on oil prices to free up more domestic production. In 1979, Carter went so far as to promise that the country would never again “use more foreign oil” than it had in 1977. Days after taking office, President Ronald Reagan eliminated the remaining federal controls on oil prices. The approach appeared to be working: By the early 1980s, U.S. oil consumption had fallen to its lowest level in more than a decade. But the conditions that encouraged conservation soon changed. Weaker oil demand and growing supply contributed to a glut that sent oil prices plunging in 1986. As oil became cheaper, the economic pressure to conserve diminished, and the efficiency gains of the previous decade began to level off. The political approach was changing too. Reagan’s administration sought deep cuts to federal conservation research, part of a broader retreat from government-led energy programs during the 1980s. Conservation had never been the country’s only answer to the oil shocks. Policy makers were simultaneously trying to increase domestic production and diversify the country’s energy supply. Carter argued in 1979 that the country needed to “produce more” as well as “conserve more.” What ultimately endured was not the ambition to wean the country off oil, but the goal of making America less vulnerable to foreign suppliers. In April, my colleague Idrees Kahloon wrote that the country is at a point where it can administer energy “shocks to other countries without feeling much pain itself,” but Americans have not been spared the effects of an international oil shortage. Gasoline prices still rise with global oil prices, regardless of where the crude comes from. Countries that are more dependent on Gulf energy, meanwhile, have borne more of the disruption. Most of the crude oil passing through Hormuz was headed to Asia , not the United States. The Philippines declared a state of emergency in response to energy shortages, Japan faced higher oil costs, and European countries saw disruptions to natural-gas shipments push prices up. This is not quite the future the Lovinses imagined, but neither is it the one they feared. They understood the calm of the 1980s as a reprieve, not a resolution. Four decades later, the United States has emerged from the crises of the ’70s as the world’s largest oil producer, far less dependent on the Middle East but still dependent on fuel itself. America may not be as vulnerable to disruptions abroad, but as long as oil is traded on a global market, the country cannot fully insulate itself from what happens beyond its borders.

items.title: L’Algérie envisage de taxer les fortunes de plus de 80 milliards de centimes dès 2027
items.description: L’Algérie envisage d'élargir la taxation des grandes fortunes à celles supérieures à 80 millions de dinars (8 milliards de centimes), à des taux allant de 0,2 à 1%. Jusque-là, seuls les patrimoines de plus de 100 millions de dinars étaient soumis à l’impôt sur la fortune. Le projet de loi de finances pour 2027 fixe les montants de l’impôt sur la fortune pour chaque catégorie de patrimoine et prévoit les sanctions à appliquer en cas de retard dans la déclaration. PLF 2027 : Taxation des fortunes de plus de 8 milliards de centimes L’article 25 du texte présenté par le gouvernement propose de modifier les dispositions des différents alinéas de l'article 281 du Code des impôts directs et taxes assimilées (CIDTA) en portant l’impôt sur le fortune aux taux suivants : 0% pour les patrimoines de moins 80.000.000 DA, 0,20% pour les fortunes de 80.000.000 à 120.000.000 DA, 0,30% de 120.000.001 à 200.000.000 DA, 0,40% de 200.000.001 à 300.000.000 DA, 0,50% de 300.000.001 à 400.000.000 DA et 1% pour les fortunes supérieures à 400.000.000 DA (40 milliards de centimes). Les sanctions prévues en cas de retard de la déclaration Le dépôt tardif de la déclaration prévue au même article entraîne l’application d’une pénalité de 10% si le retard n’excède pas un mois, de 20% lorsque le retard excède un mois et n’excède pas deux mois et de 25% lorsque le retard excède deux mois. Le contribuable qui n’a pas souscrit la déclaration est taxé d’office et sa cotisation est majorée de 25%, après avoir été mis en demeure de la produire dans un délai de trente jours. Si la déclaration est produite dans ce délai de trente jours, la majoration est ramenée à 20%. Un faible taux de recouvrement entre 2022 et 2025 Le gouvernement explique que depuis la refonte de l’impôt sur la fortune (ISF) à la faveur de la loi de Finances pour 2020, la contribution dudit dispositif en matière de recouvrement reste “négligeable”. Sur la période 2022-2025, les recettes annuelles de cet impôt varient entre 20 et 25 millions de dinars. C'est pourquoi, lit-on dans l’exposé des motifs, il est proposé d’élargir l’assiette d’imposition à l’ISF, en révisant le seuil d’assujettissement de 100.000.000 DA à 80.000.000 DA. Il est également proposé de réviser le barème progressif de l’ISF, afin de permettre une plus grande contribution des personnes à haut patrimoine au financement du budget de l’État, et ce, “eu égard à leur capacité contributive”, explique le gouvernement. L’article L'Algérie envisage de taxer les fortunes de plus de 80 milliards de centimes dès 2027 est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Alerte météo | Pluies orageuses dès cette nuit : Les zones concernées
items.description: L'Institut national de la météorologie alerte sur un changement important marqué par de fortes pluies orageuses et une baisse sensible des températures dès la nuit de ce jeudi 8 octobre 2026. . Des précipitations temporairement orageuses et localement abondantes toucheront d'abord les zones côtières du Nord et l'extrême Nord-Ouest de la Tunisie. Ces intempéries s'étendront progressivement au cours de la journée du vendredi 9 octobre à l'ensemble du Nord, du Centre et localement au Sud du pays. ​Les prévisions font état de cumuls de pluie particulièrement importants dans les gouvernorats de Zaghouan, Siliana, Sidi Bouzid, Kairouan ainsi que dans la région du Sahel. Les quantités d'eau oscillent généralement entre 30 et 50 mm, pouvant atteindre localement jusqu'à 70 mm. Ces précipitations s'accompagneront de chutes de grêle par endroits et de fortes rafales de vent lors de l'apparition des nuages orageux. ​Parallèlement, une baisse marquée du mercure est attendue, en particulier sur le Nord de la Tunisie avec des maximales qui ne dépasseront pas les 20 à 24 °C en général, s'abaissant à 18 °C sur les hauteurs. Y. N. L’article Alerte météo | Pluies orageuses dès cette nuit : Les zones concernées est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Falsification présumée du scrutin à Tanger : L’instruction accélère, Limouri attendu devant le juge
items.description: L’enquête judiciaire sur l’affaire présumée de falsification de bulletins de vote lors des élections législatives du 23 septembre dans la circonscription de Tanger-Assilah a franchi une nouvelle étape jeudi. La Cour d’appel de Tanger a ouvert les premières auditions approfondies des personnes poursuivies dans ce dossier qui continue d’alimenter le débat public au Maroc. Selon des sources informées qui se sont confiées à Hespress , le juge d’instruction a convoqué quatre des sept mis en cause placés en détention provisoire afin de les entendre dans le cadre de l’instruction détaillée. Cette procédure vise à éclaircir les circonstances de l’affaire et à établir les responsabilités de chacun dans ce qui est considéré comme l’un des épisodes les plus sensibles du dernier scrutin législatif. Parmi les personnes poursuivies figure Mounir Limouri, président du Conseil communal de Tanger et coordinateur provincial du Parti Authenticité et Modernité (PAM). Toutefois, le maire de la ville n’a pas été entendu lors de cette première journée d’auditions. D’après les mêmes sources, son interrogatoire détaillé devrait avoir lieu la semaine prochaine. Les quatre personnes entendues jeudi sont les présidents de deux bureaux de vote ainsi que leurs adjoints à l’école Al-Qods, située dans le quartier populaire de Casabarata, au centre de Tanger. C’est dans ces bureaux que se seraient déroulés les faits à l’origine de l’enquête. Le juge d’instruction a également procédé à plusieurs confrontations entre les prévenus afin de clarifier certains éléments du dossier et de lever les zones d’ombre qui subsistent encore autour du déroulement des événements. La défense a, pour sa part, sollicité un report des auditions afin de pouvoir consulter le dossier judiciaire, à l’exception d’un seul accusé. À l’issue de l’audience, le magistrat instructeur a décidé de reporter l’ensemble des auditions approfondies à la semaine prochaine, une échéance qui pourrait permettre de mieux cerner les contours de l’affaire. Des accusations lourdes contre le maire de Tanger Dans le cadre de cette procédure, le juge d’instruction a retenu à l’encontre de Mounir Limouri plusieurs chefs d’accusation liés aux opérations électorales. Il lui est notamment reproché d’avoir porté atteinte au déroulement du scrutin dans le but de modifier ou de tenter d’en modifier les résultats. Il est également poursuivi pour participation à la falsification d’un document public ainsi que pour corruption, à travers des offres, promesses ou avantages destinés à obtenir l’accomplissement d’un acte. Selon les informations recueillies par Hespress , ces poursuites s’appuient sur l’article 58 de la loi organique n°27.11 relative à la Chambre des représentants, ainsi que sur les articles 352, 353, 251 et 129 du Code pénal. En application des articles 152 et 153 du Code de procédure pénale, le juge d’instruction a ordonné son placement en détention provisoire. Mounir Limouri avait été écroué jeudi dernier après près de 72 heures passées en garde à vue. Son interpellation était intervenue à l’aéroport Tanger-Ibn Battouta, immédiatement après son arrivée en provenance de Malaga, en Espagne, dans le cadre de l’exécution d’un mandat de recherche national lié à cette affaire. Une enquête partie d’un sac de bulletins de vote L’origine du dossier remonte à la journée électorale du 23 septembre. Ce jour-là, un individu avait été surpris en possession d’un sac contenant des bulletins de vote provenant d’un bureau installé à l’école Al-Qods, dans le quartier de Kasabrata. Cette découverte avait conduit les enquêteurs à élargir leurs investigations afin de déterminer l’origine de ces documents et les circonstances de leur sortie puis de leur réintégration au sein du bureau de vote concerné. Les investigations ont ensuite conduit les autorités vers un établissement hôtelier de Tanger, où les éléments recueillis ont fait apparaître la présence de Mounir Limouri aux côtés d’autres personnes impliquées dans l’affaire. Les expertises techniques réalisées dans le cadre de l’enquête ont permis de récupérer des images de vidéosurveillance qui avaient été effacées. Les enquêteurs ont également procédé à l’analyse de téléphones portables, de communications téléphoniques et des objets saisis. Selon les conclusions préliminaires de l’enquête, les enregistrements vidéo et les expertises techniques ont établi un lien entre les deux sacs aperçus dans l’établissement hôtelier et ceux saisis dans le cadre de la procédure. Les investigations ont également mis en évidence des échanges et communications entre Mounir Limouri et d’autres suspects avant le scrutin ainsi qu’au cours de son déroulement. The post Falsification présumée du scrutin à Tanger : L’instruction accélère, Limouri attendu devant le juge appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Burkina | Budget 2027 : L’avant-projet de loi de finance table sur 4 200 milliards FCFA
items.description: ‎(Ouagadougou, 8 octobre 2026). Le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ a présidé, ce jeudi l’hebdomadaire Conseil des ministres. Le Ministre Porte-parole du Gouvernement, Camarade Pingdwendé Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO, indique que le Conseil a examiné et adopté plusieurs dossiers et pris d'importantes décisions pour la bonne marche de la Nation et pour le plein épanouissement des Burkinabè, conformément à la vision de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire. ‎ ‎Au titre du Ministère de l’Économie et des Finances, le Conseil a adopté un avant-projet de loi de finances exercice 2027. Selon le Camarade Ministre de l’Économie et des Finances, Dr Aboubakar NACANABO, le budget exercice 2027 s’élève à 4 200 milliards FCFA en recettes contre 4 800 milliards FCFA en dépenses. Ce budget conformément au plan R.E.L.A.N.C.E., va booster la croissance, en accompagnant le secteur agricole, l’industrialisation, l’équipement des Forces Armées nationales, l’amélioration des secteurs sociaux de base. Cet avant-projet de loi de finances qui sera transmis à l’Assemblée législative du Peuple, a prévu des allègements fiscaux pour la vente des œufs, pour les agences de voyages et les sociétés d’État, en révisant le Code général des impôts, selon Dr Aboubakar NACANABO. ‎ ‎La Ligue de la souveraineté pour développer le sport ‎ ‎Pour le compte de la Présidence du Faso, le Conseil a adopté deux dossiers majeurs. Le Premier dossier est relatif à la création d’une compétition en football, dénommée « La Ligue de la souveraineté ». ‎La Ministre des Sports, de la Jeunesse et de l’Emploi, Camarade Annick Lydie Djouma PIKBOUGOUM/ZINGUÉ OUATTARA soutient que ce championnat s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’Initiative présidentielle pour la Relève et la Promotion de l'Élite sportive. Elle souligne que la Ligue de la souveraineté traduit la volonté du Gouvernement de rapprocher davantage la haute compétition de toutes les régions sportives. Cette ligue a pour mission essentielle d'assurer une meilleure répartition géographique de l'offre sportive sur l'ensemble du territoire national. ‎« En termes d'organisation, nous allons avoir 20 équipes, soit une équipe par région et trois équipes pour la région du Kadiogo et deux équipes pour la région du Guiriko », a-t-elle précisé. ‎ 20 Centres médicaux communaux, 20 maternités modernes, 4 blocs opératoires et un Institut du cœur ‎ ‎Toujours pour le compte de la Présidence du Faso, le Conseil a validé la liste des projets du Bureau National des Grands Projets du Burkina et ce, dans le cadre de l’Initiative Présidentielle pour la Santé (IPS) dont l’objectif est de réformer le système de santé à travers l'amélioration de l'offre de santé et de l'accessibilité des soins de santé pour les Burkinabè. « L'adoption de la liste des projets permettra de construire et d'équiper 20 Centres médicaux communaux, 20 maternités modernes, 4 blocs opératoires au profit de l'hôpital militaire Halassane-Coulibaly et un institut du cœur », a précisé le Ministre Porte-parole du Gouvernement, Camarade Pingdwendé Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO. ‎ ‎Direction de la communication de la Présidence du Faso Minute.bf

items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · " style="width: 100%; min-height: 50px; max-height: 30000px; border: none; overflow: hidden; display: block;" scrolling="no"> The government on Thursday raised the price of petrol by Rs2.31 per litre, and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.78 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs398.96 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs395.72 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 9 (Friday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: What I Saw at New York’s Anti-Israel October 7 Rallies
items.description: Yesterday was a reminder of the difficulty that the pro-Palestine left has with showing grace even for the dead. On the third anniversary of the day that Hamas gunmen and freelance killers arrived in Israel on motorcycles and paragliders and trucks, and slaughtered children and grandparents and mothers and fathers and dancing young people, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani put out a statement that was empathetic and modulated in tone … for about 50 words. “This day is profoundly painful for so many New Yorkers,” Mamdani began. “It marks three years since the horrific war crimes of October 7. On that day, Hamas killed more than 1,100 Israelis and abducted 251 others. We grieve alongside our many friends and neighbors who still carry that unthinkable loss.” Alas, then came the next 162 words, as the young mayor indulged his anger with Israel. He apparently felt obligated to give New York City—which is home to the biggest Jewish population of any city on the globe—a history lesson that seemed to suggest that Israel brought the October 7 tragedy upon itself. “The suffering did not begin nor end that day,” he wrote. “It instead continued through the Israeli government’s devastating, ongoing genocide in Gaza, in which it has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians—including more than 21,000 children. Even since the so-called ceasefire, more than 1,400 Palestinians have been killed. That suffering has intensified with every Israeli bomb dropped on ambulances waiting outside hospitals, every drone strike targeting a residential building or journalist, and every shipment of food aid turned away at a border crossing.” [ Jonathan Chait: Progressive activists are sometimes on the wrong side of history ] On he went, referencing Israeli war crimes and apartheid and unbearable grief and American complicity in it all. By the time he concluded, he had turned grace into a cudgel. Ammiel Hirsch, a prominent New York rabbi and a longtime peace advocate, called the statement “morally perverse” and likened it to “sticking a knife into the pain of the Jewish community.” Mamdani might have thought his statement to be provocative enough to satisfy even the most anti-Zionist, anti-Israel leftist. But portions of New York’s pro-Palestine community were insistent about observing the anniversary with a Citywide Protest Resisting Genocide since 1948 . They were less intent on remembering Palestinians who have suffered grievously than they were focused on implicitly saluting Hamas’s savage attack, as their call to protest offered “glory to the martyrs, victory to the resistance.” And a fringe went further still, denouncing Mamdani for what it perceived as insufficient anti-Israel fervor. I spent some hours yesterday tracking these protests, including classroom walkouts and marches, and in truth, the numbers were deeply underwhelming. The demonstration began with 80 or so New York University students gathering for a noontime rally in Washington Square Park. They chanted, denounced their university leaders, and listened as an NYU professor spun out various conspiracy theories suggesting that Israel was principally responsible for its own casualties. Two hours later, another 75 or 80 students gathered on Broadway, outside the Columbia University campus, and chanted, “Intifada revolution” and “Palestine from river to sea,” an idea that, as a practical matter, would entail the abolition of Israel. A larger rally was planned at City Hall Park in the late afternoon. Protesters there numbered—and my grading could be generous—a touch more than 200. This included a breakaway group of roughly two dozen anti-Zionist ultra-Orthodox Satmars, a crew of black-clad anarchists who did their best to appear forbidding, and an impressively insistent Maoist Communist faction. The lackluster turnout might have owed in part to the fact that the grandees of New York’s organized left, in particular the New York City chapter of Democratic Socialists of America, were savvy enough to avoid militant protest on this solemn day. The New York City DSA went silent on social media, making no mention of October 7 or the rallies. Only the youth wing of DSA showed up. [ Rose Horowitch: Where are all the campus protests? ] There was a faint hint of anti-Mamdanism. A young protester, his face wrapped in a keffiyeh, shouted into a bullhorn and assayed a brief attack on the mayor. His voice was muffled by the cloth, so it was difficult to make out what he said, save for the fact that he repeated it rhythmically. Perhaps seven or eight protesters joined in, and a Maoist held aloft and jiggled an anti-Mamdani sign. The atmosphere grew more hostile as day turned to night and the protest came to a desultory end. According to news reports, a rump group of perhaps 100 followers of various obscure militant-left groups and pro-Palestine groups marched north from city hall to Union Square. They were intent on disrupting a remembrance run by the anti-war group Israelis for Peace and attended by Mamdani. That vigil recognized both the Israeli dead and the many thousands of Palestinians who have died in the war in Gaza. The protesters crowded in, unleashing boos and chants, not least at Mamdani, whom they appeared to cast as Judas for standing alongside left-wing Jews and very liberal Zionists. Peter Sterne, an editor at City & State New York , posted on X some of their nastier chants: “Traitor, traitor, come on out! You sold all your people out!” and “Zohran, you can’t hide. We charge you with genocide!” Mamdani, accompanied by his police detail, left to a chorus of jeers and boos . A revolution eating its own is a historical commonplace. For now, Mamdani has used his considerable political skills to keep the most uncompromising of his pro-Palestine-left supporters in check. But last night perhaps signaled a fraying of patience.

items.title: Rising food prices and poor rains fuel fears of hunger crisis in Darfur
items.description: Rising food prices, declining rainfall and mounting economic pressures are deepening hardship across Sudan’s Darfur region, fuelling fears of worsening food shortages as displacement and the destruction of agricultural livelihoods compound the humanitarian crisis. In West Darfur, particularly the state capital El Geneina, soaring food prices , expensive imports and currency fluctuations have placed further pressure on households. Journalist Mohiuddin Zakaria told Radio Dabanga that the price of a sack of millet had doubled from about SDG300,000 to SDG600,000. Prices of sorghum , cooking oil and other essential commodities have also risen sharply. Zakaria attributed the increases partly to poor rainfall and what he described as attempts by some traders to monopolise essential goods, warning that declining agricultural production could push the state towards a severe food crisis and possibly famine. West Darfur relies heavily on food supplies imported through neighbouring Chad . Zakaria said the price of 1,000 Chadian francs had risen from about SDG35,000 a month ago to around SDG46,000, making imported goods more expensive. High transaction costs through the Bank of Khartoum’s Bankak application have added to the burden. Zakaria said the discount rate in the state had reached approximately 46 per cent, while one resident reported an exchange rate of SDG70,000 through the application. Zakaria said disruptions in the currency market , growing reliance on the parallel market to determine the exchange rate between the Sudanese pound and the Chadian franc, and fluctuations in the dollar’s value had all contributed to rising commodity prices and increased economic pressure on residents. In North Darfur, however, the agricultural outlook appears more promising in some areas. Sheikh Mohammed Bakr Suleiman, an administrator in the El Hamra area south of Kutum, described this year’s agricultural season as promising. Speaking to Radio Dabanga, Suleiman praised the authorities for providing farmers with agricultural machinery and equipment, which he said had improved productivity. However, he said the area had also received large numbers of people displaced by fighting in El Fasher. Many own agricultural land but need access to essential services. Saleh Mahmoud, head of the Darfur Bar Association, warned that insufficient rainfall threatened the agricultural season and could further deepen Sudan’s humanitarian crisis . He called on the international community to impose a 90-day truce and compel both sides in the war to halt hostilities, allowing humanitarian organisations to deliver aid to displacement camps and other affected areas. Mahmoud said the Darfur Bar Association had issued a statement warning that the situation was more critical than before, with the lives of millions of Sudanese people at risk. He said the war had destroyed villages, homes, crops and farms across Darfur, Kordofan and Blue Nile, as well as the gum arabic belt, undermining food production and livelihoods. The destruction has left millions dependent on urgent humanitarian assistance, he added, warning that some areas had officially entered famine. On behalf of the Darfur Bar Association, Mahmoud urged Sudanese people and the international community to press both sides to end the war immediately. Share article The post Rising food prices and poor rains fuel fears of hunger crisis in Darfur appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .

items.title: White vs traditional marriage: Aesthetics above culture?
items.description: “I don’t believe a white wedding is necessary. I believe our traditional marriages are beautiful and complete. Yet, when I imagine my own wedding, I still picture myself in a white dress. My view that a white wedding is unnecessary is driven by the Pan-Africanism and love for Ghanaian culture in me, yet my interest in the white wedding is driven by the beauty that comes with it. In Ghana, marriage does not begin with a bride walking down an aisle. It can begin with a knock at the door. Across Ghana’s ethnic groups, traditional marriage ceremonies may differ in name and detail, but they share a common thread: marriage is not treated as a union between two individuals alone, but as a coming together of families. Among the Akan, this is known as kɔkɔɔkɔ, while the Ewe refer to their form of knocking as vɔƒoƒo. The Ga have Agboshimɔ, followed by rites involving acceptance, the presentation of a cover cloth, and traditional food. Among the Mole-Dagbani, customs include Diɛŋ, Nyuyu ɲmabu, Dɔyiripaya and payipin, while traditions among the Guan vary across their different communities. Despite these differences, the ceremonies generally involve families formally meeting, seeking approval, and presenting gifts or items as part of the marriage process. Then came another form of marriage: the white wedding, which involves the aisle, the white dress, the church, the vows and the words, “By the power vested in me…” And somehow, for many Ghanaians, the white wedding has become the picture many people grow up imagining when they think of what a “proper” wedding should look like. After families have gathered to recognise the union, another ceremony often follows, one in which the couple publicly makes vows to each other. Mary, a university student, says she would like to experience a white wedding because she finds them beautiful and likes the idea of wearing a gown. Like other Ghanaian women interviewed for this story, she does not consider the white wedding necessary, viewing it instead as an aesthetic choice. Marriage Under the Ordinance According to the Judicial Service of Ghana, the Marriage Ordinance, Cap. 127 provides the statutory framework for marriages under the Ordinance. An ordinance marriage is monogamous, while a customary marriage is potentially polygamous. The Judicial Service notes that marriages conducted under the Ordinance have the same legal validity whether they take place in an orthodox church, metropolitan assembly or court. In other words, an ordinance marriage does not become legally valid simply because there is a white gown, a church, an aisle or a bridal train. Yet for some Ghanaians, the appeal of the white wedding extends beyond its legal status. For Sarah, a university graduate, it is largely about the beauty and emotion associated with the ceremony. “I feel like it is just beautiful, being in your white dress and having your daddy or this man walking you down the aisle with your man standing there. Like those ones where the groom sees you and he starts crying? How crazy, but yeah, it is beautiful. A white wedding is beautiful, so that’s what appeals to me.” But aesthetics are not the only factor. For Sarah, her Christian faith also influences her desire for a white wedding. “I am a Christian, and a white wedding is not all the time, but most of the time it takes place in a church. And there’s this man of God blessing your marriage, and it’s like you are getting married in front of God, like God is in your union, and I feel like that is good, that is beautiful. So, I’d say yes, maybe my religion is part of why I may want a white wedding.” For some Christians, therefore, the church ceremony carries significance beyond the aesthetics of the wedding. Some churches have specific requirements concerning marriage, where couples who have not undergone a church wedding cannot take the Holy Communion. Does the Bible Require a White Wedding? The Bible contains several passages that speak about marriage, companionship, and the responsibilities of husbands and wives. Genesis 2:24 speaks of a man leaving his father and mother and holding fast to his wife, while Ecclesiastes 4:9 describes the value of two people working together. Proverbs 18:22 speaks positively of finding a wife, and Ephesians 5:25 instructs husbands to love their wives. These passages affirm marriage and the responsibilities that come with it, but they do not prescribe a specific modern wedding format, whether a couple must marry in a church, wear a white gown, walk down an aisle, or have a particular type of ceremony. There is nothing wrong with a white wedding; in fact, it is beautiful, sophisticated and memorable. What matters is the couple involved, their financial readiness, and their motivation for desiring both the traditional and white wedding.

items.title: Tumu Municipal Hospital receives new delivery bed to boost maternity care
items.description: The Tumu Municipal Hospital’s Maternity unit has received a new delivery bed and light to support its operations. Almost all the beds in the ward have broken down, making it extremely difficult for health workers to provide women in labour with a suitable and comfortable place to deliver. However, the challenge has been slightly eased with the provision of a new bed by a group of individuals who describe themselves as friends of the Member of Parliament. The Tumu Municipal Hospital continues to grapple with several challenges, including the absence of a dedicated children’s ward and a deplorable maternity ward. The beds in the ward are not only in poor condition but are also too small to comfortably accommodate women during delivery. Acting Nurse Manager at the facility, Cicelia Haluri Iddrisu, says the situation is putting considerable strain on the hospital’s operations. She explained that the limited space in the maternity ward makes it difficult for the facility to accommodate more women at the same time. “The ward generally is so old, and we don’t have most of the equipment that we need to use. The space too is so small, so if you have three or four women coming in, it’s difficult to get all of them into that space, and there’s also no privacy in the room,” she said. But there is now some relief for women using the delivery room, as friends of the Member of Parliament for Sissala East have donated a well-furnished delivery bed to the facility. For the donors, seeing people in the area struggle to access proper care due to the poor state of the ward prompted them to support the hospital. “I see people in need, and we decided to come and help”, Funda Gocuk said. “The government should be giving the help, but they don’t always do it. Therefore, people of the North always tend to suffer. So, this time round, we decided to go for maternity care, and hopefully this will help the women here,” Sandra Kodimah added. Receiving the donation on behalf of the Medical Superintendent, Dr Raymond Danso, Head of Pharmacy, Johnson Yandanbil, commended the donors for the gesture, describing it as a timely intervention. He, however, noted that the hospital continues to face several other challenges that require urgent attention. “Tumu Hospital is one of the referral hospitals in this Municipality, and so we conduct over 100 deliveries in a month. So, this particular intervention has come at the right time. However, we also lack a Children’s ward and other facilities, and we call for urgent intervention,” he said. The Member of Parliament, Mohammed Issah Bataglia, expressed gratitude to the three individuals for their support and assured the hospital of further interventions to help address some of its outstanding needs. “I sincerely do appreciate their efforts. They’re doing very little things that are having a great impact on the people,” he noted.
